Apple___Apple_scab.name: Apple - Apple scab
Apple___Apple_scab.cause: Fungus Venturia inaequalis; spreads in cool, wet spring weather.
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to dark velvety spots on leaves and fruit; leaves may yellow and drop.
treatment: Spray a protective fungicide (e.g. captan or mancozeb) from bud break through wet periods.
Remove and destroy badly infected leaves.
prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn.
Plant scab-resistant varieties; prune for airflow.

Apple___Black_rot.name: Apple - Black rot
Apple___Black_rot.cause: Fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa; survives in dead wood and dried fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Purple-edged leaf spots ('frog-eye'), rotting fruit, sunken cankers on branches.
treatment: Prune out cankered and dead branches.
Apply a fungicide such as captan during the growing season.
prevention: Remove mummified fruit from the tree and ground.
Keep trees vigorous and avoid wounding bark.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.name: Apple - Cedar apple rust
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Fungus Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae; needs nearby juniper (cedar) trees to complete its life cycle.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surface, later with tiny tubes underneath.
treatment: Apply a fungicide such as myclobutanil from pink bud stage through early summer.
Remove heavily infected leaves.
prevention: Remove nearby junipers or their galls where possible.
Plant rust-resistant apple varieties.

Apple___healthy.name: Apple - Healthy
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Keep monitoring leaves regularly, especially after wet weather.
Clean up fallen leaves and prune for airflow.

Blueberry___healthy.name: Blueberry - Healthy
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Keep monitoring leaves regularly.
Maintain acidic, well-drained soil and good airflow.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.name: Cherry - Powdery mildew
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.cause: Fungus Podosphaera clandestina; favoured by warm days, cool nights and high humidity.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery patches on young leaves; leaves may curl and pucker.
treatment: Spray sulphur or potassium bicarbonate at first signs.
Remove badly infected shoots.
prevention: Prune to open the canopy and improve airflow.
Avoid excess nitrogen fertiliser, which promotes soft growth.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.name: Cherry - Healthy
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Keep monitoring leaves regularly.
Prune for airflow and remove fallen leaves.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.name: Corn - Gray leaf spot (Cercospora)
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.cause: Fungus Cercospora zeae-maydis; survives in crop residue; favoured by warm, humid weather.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Long, narrow, rectangular grey-tan lesions running between leaf veins.
treatment: Apply a fungicide (strobilurin or triazole group) if disease appears before tasselling.
Consult an expert if spreading quickly.
prevention: Rotate crops (avoid corn after corn).
Plant resistant hybrids; manage infected residue.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.name: Corn - Common rust
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.cause: Fungus Puccinia sorghi; spores blow in on the wind during cool, moist weather.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small, raised, cinnamon-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces.
treatment: Fungicide is usually only worthwhile if rust appears early and severely.
Monitor spread before spraying.
prevention: Plant rust-resistant hybrids.
Plant early to avoid peak rust conditions.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.name: Corn - Northern leaf blight
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.cause: Fungus Exserohilum turcicum; survives in crop residue; favoured by moderate temperatures and long dew periods.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions on leaves.
treatment: Apply a fungicide around tasselling if lesions are spreading to upper leaves.
prevention: Plant resistant hybrids.
Rotate crops and manage infected residue.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.name: Corn - Healthy
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Keep monitoring leaves regularly.
Rotate crops each season.

Grape___Black_rot.name: Grape - Black rot
Grape___Black_rot.cause: Fungus Guignardia bidwellii; survives in dried, shrivelled berries (mummies).
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown circular leaf spots with dark borders; berries shrivel into hard black mummies.
treatment: Apply a fungicide (e.g. mancozeb or myclobutanil) from early shoot growth until berries begin to colour.
Remove infected leaves and berries.
prevention: Remove all mummified berries from vines and ground.
Prune for airflow and sunlight.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).name: Grape - Esca (Black measles)
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).cause: A complex of wood-rotting fungi that infect the trunk through pruning wounds.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' yellow or red patches between leaf veins; dark spots on berries; vines may suddenly collapse.
treatment: There is no cure; cut out infected wood well below visible damage.
Remove and destroy severely affected vines.
prevention: Prune in dry weather and protect large pruning wounds.
Disinfect pruning tools between vines.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.name: Grape - Leaf blight (Isariopsis leaf spot)
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.cause: Fungus Pseudocercospora vitis (Isariopsis clavispora); favoured by warm, humid conditions.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown spots on leaves, which may merge; early leaf drop.
treatment: Spray a fungicide such as mancozeb or a copper-based product.
Remove infected leaves.
prevention: Prune for airflow and avoid wetting leaves.
Clean up fallen leaves after the season.

Grape___healthy.name: Grape - Healthy
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Keep monitoring leaves regularly.
Prune for airflow and sunlight.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).name: Orange - Huanglongbing (Citrus greening)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).cause: Bacterium Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus, spread by the Asian citrus psyllid insect.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Blotchy, uneven yellowing of leaves; small, lopsided, bitter fruit; tree declines over years.
treatment: There is no cure; remove and destroy infected trees to protect nearby trees.
Control psyllid insects with recommended insecticides.
prevention: Plant only certified disease-free nursery stock.
Monitor regularly for psyllids and report suspected cases to agriculture officials.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.name: Peach - Bacterial spot
Peach___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterium Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni; spreads in rain and wind, especially on sandy soils.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark angular spots on leaves that fall out ('shot-hole'); spots and cracks on fruit.
treatment: Apply copper-based sprays, mainly during the dormant season and early spring.
Remove severely infected twigs.
prevention: Plant resistant varieties.
Keep trees healthy with balanced fertilisation.

Peach___healthy.name: Peach - Healthy
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Keep monitoring leaves regularly.
Prune for airflow.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.name: Bell pepper - Bacterial spot
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.cause: Xanthomonas bacteria; spread by infected seed, rain splash and handling wet plants.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown; leaves yellow and drop.
treatment: Spray copper-based products (often mixed with mancozeb) at first symptoms.
Remove badly infected plants.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants.
Avoid overhead watering; don't handle plants when wet; rotate crops.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.name: Bell pepper - Healthy
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Keep monitoring leaves regularly.
Water at the base of plants and rotate crops.

Potato___Early_blight.name: Potato - Early blight
Potato___Early_blight.cause: Fungus Alternaria solani; survives in soil and crop debris; attacks older, stressed leaves first.
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings ('target' pattern), usually on lower leaves first.
treatment: Spray a fungicide such as mancozeb or chlorothalonil.
Remove infected lower leaves.
prevention: Rotate crops (avoid potato and tomato in the same field each year).
Keep plants well fed and watered to reduce stress.

Potato___Late_blight.name: Potato - Late blight
Potato___Late_blight.cause: Phytophthora infestans, a fungus-like water mould; spreads very fast in cool, wet weather.
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, dark, water-soaked patches on leaves, often with white growth underneath; tubers rot.
treatment: Act immediately: remove and destroy infected plants.
Spray a recommended fungicide for late blight (e.g. metalaxyl + mancozeb or cymoxanil + mancozeb) and consult an expert.
prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers and resistant varieties.
Avoid overhead irrigation; keep potatoes away from tomatoes.

Potato___healthy.name: Potato - Healthy
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Keep monitoring leaves, especially in cool, wet weather (late blight risk).
Rotate crops each season.

Raspberry___healthy.name: Raspberry - Healthy
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Keep monitoring leaves regularly.
Thin canes for airflow.

Soybean___healthy.name: Soybean - Healthy
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Keep monitoring leaves regularly.
Rotate crops each season.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.name: Squash - Powdery mildew
Squash___Powdery_mildew.cause: Fungus Podosphaera xanthii; favoured by dry days with high humidity and crowded plants.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery spots on leaves that spread to cover them; leaves yellow and die.
treatment: Spray sulphur, potassium bicarbonate or neem oil at first signs.
Remove badly infected leaves.
prevention: Space plants well and grow in full sun.
Plant mildew-resistant varieties.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.name: Strawberry - Leaf scorch
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.cause: Fungus Diplocarpon earlianum; spreads by rain splash in warm, wet weather.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Many small dark purple spots on leaves; leaves look scorched and dry up.
treatment: Remove infected leaves.
Apply a fungicide such as captan if the disease is spreading.
prevention: Plant resistant varieties; don't crowd plants.
Water at the base; renovate old beds after harvest.

Strawberry___healthy.name: Strawberry - Healthy
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Keep monitoring leaves regularly.
Water at the base and space plants well.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.name: Tomato - Bacterial spot
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.cause: Xanthomonas bacteria; spread by infected seed, rain splash and handling wet plants.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, greasy-looking spots on leaves and fruit.
treatment: Spray copper-based products at first symptoms.
Remove badly infected plants.
prevention: Use disease-free seed and transplants.
Avoid overhead watering; rotate crops.

Tomato___Early_blight.name: Tomato - Early blight
Tomato___Early_blight.cause: Fungus Alternaria solani; survives in soil and debris; attacks older leaves first.
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings ('target' pattern) and yellow halos on lower leaves.
treatment: Spray a fungicide such as mancozeb or chlorothalonil.
Remove infected lower leaves.
prevention: Mulch soil to stop spores splashing onto leaves; stake plants.
Rotate crops; avoid planting after potato or tomato.

Tomato___Late_blight.name: Tomato - Late blight
Tomato___Late_blight.cause: Phytophthora infestans, a fungus-like water mould; spreads very fast in cool, wet weather.
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, dark, greasy patches on leaves and stems; white growth underneath in humid weather; fruit rots.
treatment: Act immediately: remove and destroy infected plants (do not compost).
Spray a recommended late blight fungicide (e.g. metalaxyl + mancozeb) and consult an expert.
prevention: Plant resistant varieties; keep tomatoes away from potatoes.
Avoid wetting leaves; space plants for airflow.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.name: Tomato - Leaf mold
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.cause: Fungus Passalora fulva; thrives in high humidity, especially in greenhouses.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale yellow spots on upper leaf surface with olive-green velvety mould underneath.
treatment: Lower humidity and improve ventilation.
Remove infected leaves; apply a fungicide such as chlorothalonil if needed.
prevention: Ventilate greenhouses; avoid wetting leaves.
Plant resistant varieties.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.name: Tomato - Septoria leaf spot
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.cause: Fungus Septoria lycopersici; spreads by rain splash; survives in plant debris.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Many small round spots with dark borders and grey-white centres, starting on lower leaves.
treatment: Remove infected lower leaves.
Spray a fungicide such as chlorothalonil or mancozeb.
prevention: Mulch soil; water at the base of plants.
Rotate crops and remove plant debris after harvest.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.name: Tomato - Spider mites (pest)
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.cause: Two-spotted spider mite (Tetranychus urticae), a tiny sap-sucking pest; thrives in hot, dry conditions.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Tiny yellow or white speckles on leaves; fine webbing underneath; leaves bronze and dry out.
treatment: Spray leaf undersides with a strong jet of water.
Use neem oil, insecticidal soap or a recommended miticide (acaricide).
prevention: Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill the mites' natural predators.
Keep plants well watered; check leaf undersides regularly.

Tomato___Target_Spot.name: Tomato - Target spot
Tomato___Target_Spot.cause: Fungus Corynespora cassiicola; favoured by warm, humid weather.
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown spots with light centres and concentric rings on leaves; can also affect fruit.
treatment: Remove infected leaves.
Spray a fungicide such as chlorothalonil or mancozeb.
prevention: Improve airflow by pruning and spacing plants.
Avoid overhead watering; remove plant debris.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.name: Tomato - Yellow leaf curl virus
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus, spread by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci).
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Leaves curl upward and turn yellow at the edges; plants are stunted and produce little fruit.
treatment: There is no cure; remove and destroy infected plants early.
Control whiteflies with yellow sticky traps and recommended insecticides.
prevention: Plant resistant varieties.
Use insect-proof nets in nurseries; remove weeds that host whiteflies.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.name: Tomato - Mosaic virus
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Tomato mosaic virus; spreads by touch, tools and infected seed; survives a long time on surfaces.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Light and dark green mottled (mosaic) pattern on leaves; leaves may be distorted.
treatment: There is no cure; remove and destroy infected plants.
Disinfect tools and wash hands after handling plants.
prevention: Plant resistant varieties and certified disease-free seed.
Avoid handling plants after using tobacco products.

Tomato___healthy.name: Tomato - Healthy
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Keep monitoring leaves regularly, especially lower leaves.
Water at the base and rotate crops.
